title: With hardship, ease
translation: Did We not open your chest for you, lift from you the burden that weighed down your back, and raise your renown? Truly, with hardship comes ease; truly, with hardship comes ease. So when you are free, strive on, and long for your Lord.
body: Is “opening the chest” an **inner widening**, or the **chest-splitting miracle** of hadith? Some exegetes, noted by Ibn Kathir, link the two; **Maududi**, citing al-Alusi, keeps them apart. The Psalmist too is “set at large” in distress; for **Luther**, such trial (**tentatio**) is the touchstone of God’s word.
question: Ease comes “with” hardship (maʿa), not after it. What might “with” say about how they belong together?
